kind: operator observation, not an executable configuration or release approval

registrar.name: Namecheap
registrar.registry_observation: v0n0.nic.ai and v0n1.nic.ai still publish the previous delegation; this is not a completed global cutover

website.certificate: Fly reports issued RSA and ECDSA certificates

preserved_failures_and_limits: The first Cloudflare authorization requested invalid zone.edit and dns.edit scopes. The corrected zone.write and dns.write request was accepted and subsequently authorized.
An earlier corrected authorization expired before approval; a fresh short local redirect allowed the owner to complete authorization.
The initial Namecheap record batch partially wrote five records and refused the sender mail-exchange record. Its actual read-back was checked; no force retry was used.
The app CNAME was then added successfully to Namecheap so the existing delegation could serve the website during migration.

One unauthenticated HTTPS probe returned curl error 7 during cutover. Subsequent direct and ordinary HTTPS probes returned 200, and the full 45-case browser check passed. The transient failure remains unexplained; no uninterrupted-availability claim is made.
The new Cloudflare root and www records replace registrar parking destinations. The old parking values are retained in the prior DNS inventory and the operator record.
Cloudflare activation, root and www HTTPS, sender verification and real account email delivery remain separate checks. No public-registration or paid-release gate is closed by this record.
